html:
The Lesotho Highlands Water Project is a system of dams and tunnels in the mountains of Lesotho that sends water to the Gauteng region of South Africa, agreed in a treaty in 1986; water began to flow in 1998.

The great Katse Dam on the Malibamatso river, finished in 1997, is one of the highest in Africa. Water flows by tunnel to the Vaal river system that serves Johannesburg and Pretoria, and the project also generates power for Lesotho.

Royalties from the water are a large source of state income, replacing some of the lost mine wages. A second phase is under way. The project became known for one of Africa's largest bribery trials, in which foreign firms were convicted of paying its chief executive. South African troops secured the dam during the intervention of 1998.
